Research Fellow - Advanced Battery Intelligence and Technology Development

The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research. 

We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee.  

Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference.  

The role

We are looking for a motivated Research Fellow to join the Electrochemical Characterization and Sensing Group at the University of Surrey, supporting an EPSRC-funded project focused on developing intelligent battery technologies.

The project aims to improve how batteries are understood, monitored and managed by combining experimental research, advanced sensing, data analysis and computational approaches. The work also involves engagement with industrial partners, with opportunities to contribute to the development and practical application of emerging battery technologies.

Depending on your background and experience, your activities may include:

Supporting the development, integration and testing of battery sensing and monitoring technologies.
Conducting electrochemical experiments, battery testing and performance evaluation.
Processing and analysing experimental data, including developing computational tools and algorithms.
Supporting experimental design, data organisation and the evaluation of battery performance.
Contributing to technical reports, research documentation and project deliverables.
Working with researchers from different disciplines to support technology development and industrial validation.

This position offers an opportunity to gain hands-on research experience, develop technical and analytical skills, and contribute to research with potential applications in battery safety, performance and future energy technologies.

This is a part-time (0.4 FTE) fixed-term position until March 2027.

About you

We welcome applications from candidates with backgrounds in engineering, materials science, chemistry, physics, computer science, data science or related disciplines.

You should have:

A relevant academic background and an interest in battery or energy technologies.
Experience or relevant knowledge in at least one of the following areas: experimental research, electrochemistry, electronic systems, data analysis, programming or computational methods.
Good analytical and problem-solving skills.
The ability to work independently and collaboratively within a research team.
Good organisational and communication skills, with attention to accurate research documentation.
How to apply

To apply, please submit your application with a CV and cover letter online via the University of Surrey jobs portal.

For an informal discussion about the position, please contact Dr Kai Yang, Advanced Technology Institute, University of Surrey, at kai.yang@surrey.ac.uk.

Click here to find out more about the benefits we offer to support you.

The University of Surrey is committed to providing an inclusive environment that offers equal opportunities for all.  We place great value on diversity and are seeking to increase the diversity within our community.  Therefore we particularly encourage applications from under-represented groups, such as people from Black, Asian and minority ethnic groups and people with disabilities.

ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY

Swansea University is a research-led university that has been making a difference since 1920. The University community thrives on exploration and discovery and offers the right balance of excellent teaching and research, matched by an enviable quality of life.

Our stunning waterfront campuses and multicultural community make us a desirable workplace for colleagues from around the world. Our reward and benefits, and ways of working enable those who join us to have enriching careers, matched by an excellent work-life balance.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The ALPHA collaboration at CERN synthesises and traps antihydrogen for precision tests of fundamental symmetry. The collaboration is world leading in precision spectroscopy and gravitational studies of antihydrogen. Following a major upgrade to the frequency metrology instrumentation in ALPHA, the aim is now to achieve or surpass the precision of spectroscopy in ordinary hydrogen. Swansea University is a founding member and a major stakeholder in the collaboration.

The successful candidate will join the Swansea team at CERN and will become a full member of the ALPHA collaboration.  The group has three permanent academic staff members, four post-doctoral staff and a varying number of PhD students actively contributing to the ALPHA project at CERN. We require the successful candidate to have a PhD in experimental physics with experience in the synthesis, laser cooling, and spectroscopy of antihydrogen, the development of Penning traps and cryogenics and microwave transport and atomic spectroscopy using microwaves

EQUALITY, DIVERSITY & INCLUSION

The University is committed to supporting and promoting equality and diversity in all its practices and activities. We aim to establish an inclusive environment and welcome diverse applications from the following protected characteristics: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (including colour, nationality, ethnic and national origin), religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation.

As an inclusive and welcoming workplace, we value people for their skills regardless of their background. Applications are welcome in Welsh and will not be treated less favourably than those submitted in English.

WELSH LANGUAGE SKILLS

The Welsh language level required for this role is Level 1 - A little. The role holder will be able to pronounce Welsh words, answer the phone in Welsh (good morning/afternoon) and use very basic everyday words and phrases (thank you, please etc.). Level 1 can be reached by completing a 1 hour course.

The University is a proud bilingual institution, our Welsh Language Strategy outlines our aspiration to promote the language and enable our staff to engage with the language as an additional workplace skill and as a gateway to new cultural and social opportunities. Applications are welcome in Welsh and will not be treated less favourably than those submitted in English. Welsh speakers have the right to an interview in Welsh. Applicants for a role where Welsh skills are essential are expected to present their application in Welsh and will be interviewed in Welsh, if shortlisted.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Applications for this role will take the format of a CV submission and cover letter.

 We are seeking a full-time Postdoctoral Research Assistant to join the Machine Learning & Articulated Robots Group (ARG) of the Oxford Robotics Institute and the Department of Engineering Science in central Oxford. The post is funded by the EPSRC’s Centre to Centre (C2C) Grant, “Mobile Robotic Inspector: Learning to Explore and Manipulate in the Real World” and is fixed-term for 24 months.

 The project will develop leaning-based approaches to contact rich mobile manipulation (LocoManipulation) with a focus on legged robots -mainly humanoids- in challenging scenarios. This C2C project is in collaboration with ETH Zurich’s “RobotX - Center for Robotics” and is build around a rich schedule of visits to and from ETH. The goal is to further develop our mobile manipulation capabilities, able of physically demanding and dexterous mobile manipulation tasks in a range of dynamic domains (industrial, service, domestic). This position will focus on using and developing learning-based perceptive approaches.

 You will develop a control framework integrating multi-modal perception and tactile feedback, for locomotion and manipulation. You will be responsible for the design, development, implementation and evaluation of learning-based loco-manipulation methods suitable for legged systems in physically-realistic simulated environments and on real robots.

 You should hold or be close to completion of a PhD/DPhil in robotics, computer science, machine learning, informatics, AI, or a closely related field. You will have an excellent academic track record in topics relevant to manipulation and locomotion; path and motion planning, whole-body control, multi-contact manipulation/locomotion, machine learning and optimisation, avatar animation or related areas. You have experience working on real robots and great team working skills.

 Informal enquiries may be addressed to Prof. Ioannis Havoutis.

 For more information about working at the Department, see  www.eng.ox.ac.uk/about/work-with-us/ 

 Only applications received before noon (12.00pm GMT) on 23 November 2026 can be considered. You will be required to upload a covering letter/supporting statement, (describing how past experience fit with the advertised position), CV and the details of two referees as part of your online application.

 These posts form part of 3-year AHRC-funded research grant, ‘Language Machines: the Arts & Humanities' Contributions to Artificial Intelligence Innovation’, led by Dr Rebecca Roach and with co-leads based at the University of Birmingham.

 Language Machines addresses four linked challenges. Firstly, the significant contributions the Arts & Humanities (A&H) have made to Artificial Intelligence (AI) innovation historically are poorly understood; Secondly, the challenges posed by generative artificial intelligences’ (GAI) transformations of our linguistic reading practices today, which require A&H expertise; thirdly, the language used to render AI today is inaccessible (high-level maths or metaphors of sentience), which impedes public understanding; Lastly, as a society we are missing out on the creative possibilities that the A&H offer for future AI innovation, usage, and regulation. The project looks both forward and back. The project’s historical component aims to recover the central (but occluded) role of the A&H in creating and analysing AI. It will map three innovative networks of experimenters working with language, meaning, reading, and machines at crucial moments before, during, and immediately after the advent of digital computing. The contemporary component utilises these historical discoveries as the basis for a series of experiments that analyse GAIs’ current reading practices, both to: develop key findings which articulate and champion the methods, expertise, and practical innovations that the A&H provide; and to utilise such innovation in the creative design and deployment of GAIs in future.

 In keeping with the broad focus of the project, applicants with expertise in humanistic modes of enquiry, and interdisciplinary working, are encouraged to apply; specialism in twentieth-century British literature and culture, book history, history of technology/STS, archival research, quantitative methods, database development, digital history, and/or Digital Humanities approaches are especially favoured.

 Main Responsibilities 

 Work within the Language Machines project, and contribute to the generation of new knowledge

 Analyse and interpret research data in a variety of formats

 Disseminate research findings for publications, research seminars, etc.

 Contribute to developing new models, techniques and methods

 Undertake management/administration arising from research

 Contribute to research-related activities and administration

 Collect research data; this may be through a variety of research methods, such as archival research, scientific experimentation, literature reviews, and research interviews

 Fosters a fair and equitable workplace for all staff

 Person Specification 

 A PhD relevant to the research area (or near completion), or equivalent PhD level qualifications

 High level analytical capability

 Ability to communicate complex information clearly

 Fluency in relevant models, theories, and methods, and ability to contribute to developing new ones

 Contribute to the planning and organising of the research project

 Co-ordinate own work with others to avoid conflict or duplication of effort and support effective collaboration

 Informal enquiries can be made to Dr Rebecca Roach, r.roach@bham.ac.uk .

 The Opportunity: 

 We are seeking a motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to advance research in Embodied AI and Spatial AI at School of Informatics, The University of Edinburgh. The position is part of a new research programme led by Dr Liang Zhao, developing AI systems that can perceive, understand, reason about, and act within three-dimensional environments.

 The successful candidate will have a PhD (or be close to completing one) in artificial intelligence, robotics, computer vision, machine learning, or a closely related field. They will undertake original research connecting spatial perception and understanding with embodied decision-making and action, developing methods that enable intelligent agents to learn from and interact with the physical world.

 Spatial intelligence, 3D scene understanding, and spatial reasoning.

 Embodied perception, mapping, and navigation.

 Multimodal foundation models and vision-language-action models.

 World models for prediction, planning, and action.

 Learning from interaction, demonstration, and reinforcement.

 Generalisation and adaptation across tasks and environments.

We are also open to considering requests for hybrid working (on a non-contractual basis) that combines a mix of remote and regular on-campus working. About the role

How does the invisible work of managing household and family life shape who participates in politics?

We are seeking a Postdoctoral Research Associate to help develop a new programme of research on the domestic mental load, gender inequality and democratic participation. You will join the Department of Politics, Languages & International Studies at the University of Bath, working with Dr Ana Catalano Weeks on the UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship project, Invisible Burdens, Visible Gaps: The Mental Load and Gendered Citizenship.

The domestic mental load involves anticipating needs, planning and coordinating everyday family life. Women undertake a disproportionate share of this work, yet its consequences for political engagement remain poorly understood. Through research in Brazil, Iceland, Italy, Japan and the UK, the project investigates how household responsibilities, gender norms and policy environments shape the mental space available for political life.

Joining at the outset, you will have an opportunity to shape the project’s qualitative research and help develop new explanations of the relationship between private life and democratic inclusion. Working closely with the principal investigator and researchers in the five countries, you will:

Help develop and refine semi-structured interview guides and creative visual methods, including participant-generated photographs (Photovoice).

Support cross-national data collection and collaboration with locally based researchers.

Lead thematic coding and analysis of interview and visual data, contributing to the project’s theoretical framework.

Develop academic publications and conference presentations, and contribute to public engagement activities.

This is an opportunity to combine substantive research leadership with close collaboration and mentoring. You will be supported to develop both collaborative and independently authored publications arising from the project, build international research relationships, and strengthen your skills in research methods and public engagement.

About you

We welcome applicants from across the social sciences. You will bring:

A PhD in political science, sociology, social policy, public policy, economics or a related discipline.

Strong qualitative research skills, including experience of interviewing and systematic coding and analysis.

An interest in gender inequalities, household labour, political engagement or related questions, and the ability to connect empirical findings to theoretical debates.

The ability to take responsibility for research tasks while working collaboratively with colleagues across countries.

Strong written and spoken English, organisational skills, and a thoughtful approach to research ethics and participant confidentiality.

Experience of comparative research, creative visual methods or qualitative analysis software such as NVivo would be an advantage. 

We welcome candidates whose expertise brings a fresh perspective to the project; prior research specifically on the mental load is not required.

Additional information

The position is full-time and fixed-term for 24 months, with scope for hybrid working. Working arrangements will be agreed with the principal investigator, balancing flexibility with in-person collaboration, participation in the department’s research community, and project activities.

As a member of Research Staff at the University of Bath, you will be encouraged to take up a minimum of 10 days professional development pro rata per year.

A lower grade offer may be made (Grade 6) with comparable reduction in responsibilities and amendment in job title to Research Assistant, if a suitable applicant cannot be found to fill the Grade 7 position. Applicants will need to be within six months of their course completion date and will be promoted to Research Associate once their PhD has been awarded. 

We consider ourselves to be a university where difference is celebrated, respected and encouraged. We have an excellent international reputation with staff from over 60 different nations and have made a positive commitment towards gender equity and intersectionality receiving a Silver Athena SWAN award. We truly believe that diversity of experience, perspectives, and backgrounds will lead to a better environment for our employees and students and encourage applications from all genders, backgrounds, and communities, particularly from under-represented groups, and value the positive impact that will have on the university. postings.advert_text:
A position exists for a Cambridge Mathematical Innovation Research Associate (CaMIRA) in the Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics to work within the recently established Cambridge Hub for Innovative Mathematics in Research and Applications (CHIMiRA). The position will be appointed at either a Research Associate or a Senior Research Associate level, depending on experience.

The purpose of CHIMiRA is to improve the real-world impact of research generated at the University of Cambridge by undertaking highly interdisciplinary academic projects, industrial collaborations, and consultancy engagements.

The successful candidate will join a small team of CaMIRAs, who typically work on a portfolio of short-to medium term projects funded by academic or industrial partners. The role will be very flexible, in both application area and project type, and the ideal candidate would necessarily be required to have developed skills in several areas of Statistics, be eager to learn techniques from different statistical disciplines, machine learning, and AI, and have excellent communication skills to scope ideas, co-design projects, and articulate statistical concepts to a non-technical audience. Prior industrial experience would be desirable, but a positive attitude to industrial engagement is essential. The role requires strong skills in interpersonal communication, relationship building, time management, manuscript preparation, and grant writing.

CHIMiRA is a self-funded Hub and requires ongoing research and industrial funding to support its research activities. Therefore, the successful candidate will be proactive in initiating collaborations with research groups throughout the University and in Industry, engaging with the wider UK Innovation Research Associate network, and communicating CHIMiRA's activities to a wide audience. They should have experience/interest in entrepreneurial activities, such as research commercialisation, intellectual property protection and/or translational research.

Duties include developing and conducting individual and collaborative research objectives, proposals, and projects. The role holder will be expected to plan and manage their own research and administration, with guidance if required, and to assist in the preparation of proposals and applications to external bodies. You must be able to communicate material of a technical nature and be able to build internal and external contacts. You may be asked to assist in the supervision of student projects, the development of student research skills, provide instruction, or plan/deliver seminars relating to the research area.

The successful candidate will have a PhD in Statistics, Data Science, or a similar discipline, may have completed a postdoctoral position or position in industry before, and possess experience in several areas of Statistics. We expect the successful candidate to have seen one or more projects through to completion, preferably with an application of their research in a real-world setting. Coding and software engineering proficiency will be expected if relevant to their experience, e.g. for machine learning challenges. Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for two years in the first instance, and the post may, subject to the availability of funding, be further renewed for a period or periods.

Preferred start date: February 2027, with mutual agreement

Interviews will likely take place in the first half of January.

Please note that we will assume that you are happy for us to approach your referees at any stage, unless you indicate otherwise in the space provided on the form.

Informal inquiries can be made by contacting Professor Sergio Bacallado de Lara at sb2116@cam.ac.uk or Professor Sofía Villar at sofia.villar@mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk.

Brunel University London was established in 1966 and is a leading multidisciplinary research-intensive technology university delivering economic, social and cultural benefits. For more information please visit: https://www.brunel.ac.uk/about/our-history/home

Description of College

The College of Engineering, Design and Physical Sciences at Brunel University of London delivers world-leading research, interdisciplinary innovation, industry engagement, and excellence in engineering, computing, design, mathematics, and physical sciences education.

Description of Role and Essential Person Specification

We are seeking a highly motivated Research Assistant or Research Fellow to contribute to CLIMABUILD, a Horizon Europe research project developing innovative methodologies, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled digital technologies and decision-support solutions to enhance the resilience, sustainability and climate adaptability of buildings and the wider built environment.

Brunel plays a leading role in research activities spanning resilience and sustainability assessment, computational modelling, lifecycle analysis, digital decision-support systems, knowledge graphs, participatory technologies and stakeholder engagement.

Working closely with the Principal Investigator and international consortium partners, the successful candidate will:

Develop, apply or support mathematical, computational and data-driven approaches for assessing the resilience, sustainability and lifecycle performance of buildings and infrastructure.
Contribute to AI-enabled digital solutions, including Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), knowledge graphs, digital twins and intelligent decision-support tools.
Investigate climate adaptation and low-carbon renovation strategies through lifecycle assessment, scenario analysis, uncertainty evaluation and multi-criteria optimisation.
Support the development, integration and validation of innovative methodologies and digital tools, working with project partners and Living Labs.
Contribute to scientific publications, project deliverables, stakeholder engagement and research dissemination.

Applicants should hold a relevant degree in Civil, Environmental, Building or Infrastructure Engineering, Computer Science or a closely related discipline. Appointment at Research Fellow level will require a PhD or equivalent research experience. Essential competencies include analytical and computational skills, programming experience (e.g. Python, MATLAB or R), knowledge of resilience, sustainability or lifecycle assessment, and familiarity with AI technologies, including LLMs. Good communication skills and the ability to work independently, with appropriate supervision according to grade, within an international and interdisciplinary team are essential.

The appointment will be made at Research Assistant or Research Fellow level, depending on the successful candidate's qualifications and experience.

We offer a generous annual leave package plus discretionary University closure days, excellent training and development opportunities as well as a great occupational pension scheme and a range of health-related support. The University is committed to a hybrid working approach.

Closing date for applications: 1 December 2026

If you have any technical issues please contact us at: hrsystems@brunel.ac.uk

 The City Law School, City St George’s, University of London, is offering a fully funded, three-year PhD scholarship for a Black British researcher commencing in September 2027. 

 We welcome applications from talented and ambitious graduates who are interested in undertaking original research in any area of law.

 We particularly encourage applications from individuals who may not previously have considered doctoral study or an academic career.

 About The City Law School 

 The City Law School is a welcoming and diverse community of scholars and students, with recognised strengths in teaching and research across a broad range of legal disciplines.

 Located in the heart of London, we are committed to academic excellence, supporting emerging researchers and creating opportunities for individuals from backgrounds historically underrepresented in doctoral research.

 Our researchers work across a wide range of legal subjects and methodologies, offering opportunities to pursue innovative research with experienced academic supervisors.

 What the scholarship offers 

 The scholarship provides:

 A full tuition fee waiver for three years.

 An annual tax-free bursary , in line with the applicable UKRI stipend rate (2027/28 amount to be confirmed).

 Up to £1,000 towards research expenses over three years, including training, equipment and conference attendance.

 Successful applicants will join The City Law School's research community and have opportunities to develop their research skills, participate in academic events and engage with researchers working in their field.

 Who can apply? 

 Applications are invited from applicants who meet the eligibility requirements for UK home-fee status and identify as Black or Black British (African, Caribbean, Other or Mixed).

 The scholarship is for full-time study, and applicants must be able to commit to a full-time doctoral programme.

 Applicants should have:

 An undergraduate degree in law (LLB or equivalent) with at least a 2:1 classification.

 Normally, a Master's degree in law or a related discipline, with at least a Merit or equivalent.

 Evidence of the ability and motivation to undertake independent, high-level research.

 We welcome research proposals across all areas of law, particularly those aligned with the expertise of our academic staff.

 You do not need to have an established academic career plan to apply. If you are interested in exploring a legal question in depth and contributing new knowledge to your field, we encourage you to consider this opportunity.

 Interested in applying? Talk to us first 

 We recognise that applying for a PhD can feel daunting, particularly if you are unfamiliar with doctoral research or have not previously considered an academic career.

 We warmly encourage prospective applicants to contact us before applying. 

 An informal conversation with our Senior Tutor for Research can help you:

 Explore whether your research idea could form the basis of a PhD.

 Identify a suitable supervisor.

 Understand what doctoral study involves.

 Develop your research proposal and prepare for the application process.

 You do not need to have a fully developed research proposal before getting in touch.

 Email: Law.PhD.Administration@city.ac.uk 

 You can also explore our research centres and academic staff profiles to learn more about our research expertise.

 How to apply 

 Please complete the form here 

 ( PhD in Law, Scholarship application )

 Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview.

 If you are currently employed by City St George's, please indicate in your application that your line manager is aware of your application.

 Application deadline: 12 noon, Friday 26 February 2027

Digit Quantitative Research Fellow

Do you have a PhD in Human Resource Management, Employment Relations, Sociology of Work and Employment, Labour Economics or related disciplines? Do you have experience of working with large, nationally representative data sets, data-linkage and relevant statistical packages such as R?. 

You will have demonstrable evidence of high-level research methods training, and, for this post specifically, advanced quantitative research skills. You will be expected to have evidence of published work of high quality, and a strong knowledge of relevant conceptual and empirical literatures relating to the digital transformation of work. Applicants with background understanding and prior research expertise of the changing nature of work and digital transformation are particularly encouraged, as are applicants with expertise in comparative study. Applicants should be willing to work on a variety of research projects and to travel, when required, for national and international meetings and dissemination and engagement activities.

Leeds University Business School is looking to recruit a Quantitative Research Fellow for the ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work (DIGIT). Digit is jointly directed by the Universities of Leeds and Sussex, in collaboration with the Universities of Manchester, Cambridge and Monash. Digit was established in 2020 and is now on its second phase research programme (2025-2029), supported by an ESRC Grant of £8.2 million. Digit brings together an interdisciplinary, international network that aims to advance understanding of how digital technologies are reshaping work, impacting on employers, employees, job seekers and governments. The centre’s core research programme is focused on digital ecosystems, and includes five research themes that investigate: fragmented digital governance; digital adoption; skills and reward, wellbeing; location and environment. Two further waves of Digit’s unique Employers’ Digital Practices at Work survey are planned. 

The Quantitative Research Fellow will work on the Digital Practices at Work Survey (DPAW), and other secondary and administrative data sets, in collaboration with Digit co-Director Professor Mark Stuart and Professor Danat Valizade, and other members of the research team. It is anticipated that the Fellow will focus on a number of projects related to analysis of DPAW and the linking of DPAW with other large-scale nationally representative datasets, such as Understanding Society, and comparator studies conducted in other countries. Topics for investigation will include: the changing trends in the adoption of digital technologies and AI on work-related issues, such as skills, rewards, work organisation and employee well-being; the impact of AI on jobs at a regional level; different trends in the nature of AI adoption by technology type between countries. There will be plenty of scope for the Fellow to help define and shape the focus on ongoing research.

 About the Role 

 The University of Warwick’s Centre for Fusion, Space and Astrophysics (CFSA) is seeking to appoint a Research Fellow for a five-year research programme focused on modelling Earth’s magnetosphere and radiation belts.

 The successful candidate will develop and apply magnetospheric, ring current, and radiation belt simulations, investigating the dynamics and coupling of these regions during geomagnetic activity. The role offers an exciting opportunity to work at the interface of space plasma physics, computational modelling, and space-weather science, within a collaborative research environment.

 This is part of a five-year multi-institution STFC-funded project entitled: why is the response of Earth’s outer radiation belt to solar wind driving so hard to predict? involving close collaboration with Northumbria University and University of Birmingham.

 In addition to conducting original research, there will be opportunity to contribute to the mentoring and supervision of PhD students within the research group as well as research grant development and capture.

 The successful candidate will be supported in pursuing their future career aspirations, including the potential to apply for promotion to the next level (Assistant Professor - Research Focussed), subject to satisfactory performance and progress and meeting the relevant promotion criteria.

 For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here) .

 About You 

 We welcome applicants with experience in either space physics, plasma physics, numerical modelling, or scientific computing. Experience with applying these to magnetospheric or radiation-belts, or similar areas, would be particularly valuable.

 If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5 (£35,302 per annum). Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6 (£36,320 per annum).

 The Centre for Fusion Space and Astrophysics is an interdisciplinary centre  embracing plasma physics applied to the grand challenges of magnetic and inertial confined fusion power, space plasma physics, solar physics, and

 astrophysics. The research spans fundamental theory, observation, and the analysis of experimental data, combined with high performance computing.

 CFSA is an established leader in plasma physics modelling, with several productions codes with global user bases, such as EPOCH and LARE. Associated space weather research spans the solar corona, heliosphere, magnetosphere, radiation belts and ionosphere as well as downstream space weather risks and impacts. Wider collaborations exist with University of Warwick’s exoplanet research group who lead the ESA Plato mission, and with Warwick Quantum to  develop novel sensing solutions for space.

 Space physics and space weather research within CFSA is supported by a diverse range of academic, government and industry stakeholders, including UKRI, UK and European Space Agencies, the Met Office, QinetiQ, EDF, AWE and Dstl. The successful candidate will have opportunities to engage with such partners through meetings, workshops and collaborative research activities, gaining valuable experience in translating fundamental research into applications with real-world impact.

THIS VACANCY IS OPEN TO INTERNAL APPLICANTS ONLY 
About us:

King's College London is one of the top 35 universities in the world and among the oldest in England. The Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience (IoPPN) is Europe's largest centre for research and teaching in mental health and the neurosciences.

The CAMHS Digital Lab is a joint initiative of South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust (SLaM), the Centre for Translational Informatics and the Department of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry. The Lab co-designs, builds and evaluates digital tools that help young people, families and clinicians understand changes in mental health and access tailored support, and conducts informatics research using the routinely collected records of NHS mental health care.

About the role:

We are seeking a Research Assistant to support the CAMHS Digital Lab's early-onset psychosis informatics programme and the platform and evaluation work associated with it. The role suits someone who is comfortable moving between routinely collected clinical data, the NHS services in which those data are generated, and the young people and families for whom the Lab's digital tools are built.

The principal workstream is the construction and validation of an electronic health record cohort of children and young people with psychosis and treatment-resistant psychosis, derived from SLaM's Clinical Record Interactive Search (CRIS) resource using structured clinical data and natural language processing, and designed to mirror the multi-centre CLEAR study of antipsychotic and clozapine treatment. You will review clinical records manually to adjudicate diagnoses and medication histories, identify false-positive cases, support linkage with educational and other administrative datasets, and contribute to the systematic reviews that frame this work. You will liaise with consultant psychiatrists, ward and community teams and research departments across SLaM and partner Trusts, and will support participant recruitment, informed consent and structured assessment where the programme requires primary data collection.

You will also support the day-to-day running of myHealthE, the Lab's caregiver- and teacher-facing data collection platform in use across SLaM and partner Trusts, providing user support to young people, families, clinicians and school staff and translating recurrent issues into improvements. The third strand of the post is qualitative: designing, conducting and analysing interviews and focus groups with young people, families and clinicians, and contributing to the Lab's co-design and public engagement work.

You will report to Professor Johnny Downs, Professor of Child Psychiatry and Health Informatics, who leads the Lab. The post has no line management responsibility, although you may support students and volunteers contributing to the workstreams. There is scope to lead or co-author publications and to develop an independent research profile in collaboration with colleagues across the IoPPN and the NIHR Maudsley Biomedical Research Centre.

This is a full time post (35 hours per week), and you will be offered a fixed term contract until 1 April 2029.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the  Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the  Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you:

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

A first degree at 2:1 or above in psychology, developmental science, health, epidemiology or a related discipline, and an MSc in mental health studies, mental health research, epidemiology or a related discipline
Experience of mental health research in an NHS or comparable clinical setting, including participant recruitment, informed consent (with consultee or personal legal representative procedures where participants may lack capacity) and administration of structured research and patient-reported assessments
Experience of working with an electronic health record research resource, such as CRIS, including manual review and validation of clinical records to adjudicate diagnoses and medication histories and to identify false-positive cases
Knowledge of the presentation, assessment and treatment of early-onset and treatment-resistant psychosis in children and young people, including antipsychotic and clozapine treatment pathways
Demonstrable competence in formal qualitative methods, from recruitment and semi-structured interviewing through to formal analysis, evidenced by peer-reviewed publication or an equivalent written output
Experience of contributing to systematic reviews, including title, abstract and full-text screening, data extraction and structured quality assessment
Experience of supporting the day-to-day running of a caregiver- or patient-facing digital data collection platform deployed in NHS services, including responding to, recording and escalating user queries
Valid Good Clinical Practice certification and Enhanced DBS clearance, or eligibility to obtain both before commencement, together with willingness to work on NHS premises with children and young people and to travel between participating sites

Desirable criteria

Doctoral training in progress or completed in a relevant field, such as psychosis, child and adolescent mental health or health informatics
Understanding of natural language processing applied to clinical text, and of linkage between health records and educational or other administrative datasets
Working knowledge of specialist statistical software (for example R, Stata or SPSS) or qualitative analysis software (for example NVivo)
Experience of working with NHS child and adolescent mental health services, including co-production or co-design activity with young people and families
Experience of contributing to applications for ethical and information governance approvals, including CRIS project amendments

Research Fellow in Fate and Effects of Emerging Contaminants in Agricultural Systems

Are you an ambitious researcher looking for your next challenge? Do you have expertise in the environmental fate and effects of emerging contaminants?

We are seeking a highly motivated Post-Doctoral Research Fellow to join the research group of Professor Laura Carter, UKRI Future Leaders Fellow, and contribute to the pioneering UK Research and Innovation-funded project, Closing the Loop: Emerging Contaminants in Agricultural Environments.

Sustainable agricultural practices, including the use of treated wastewater for irrigation and organic waste-derived soil amendments, are increasingly being adopted to address global challenges such as water scarcity and the need to reduce reliance on synthetic fertilisers. However, these approaches can inadvertently introduce emerging contaminants into agricultural systems. Understanding the environmental and human health implications of these contaminants is therefore critical as their use becomes more widespread.

This project will investigate the fate, uptake, and effects of emerging contaminants in agricultural systems, with a particular focus on pharmaceuticals. Through a mechanistic understanding of contaminant behaviour in agro-ecosystems, the research will provide new insights into how these substances influence soil health, crop productivity, and potential human exposure through food consumption. By integrating expertise across environmental chemistry, plant and soil sciences, and human health, the project aims to transform how environmental risks associated with emerging contaminants are assessed.

Working within a collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment at the University of Leeds, you will design and deliver a programme of innovative research examining contaminant uptake, transformation, and biological effects in agricultural systems. The outcomes will help inform sustainable agricultural practices and future environmental risk assessment frameworks.

We are looking for an enthusiastic and talented researcher with a background in Environmental Chemistry, Environmental Science, Environmental Biology, or a closely related discipline. You should hold a PhD and have experience in environmental contaminant research, alongside a strong interest in understanding and addressing the environmental risks posed by emerging contaminants.

What we offer in return

26 days holiday plus approx.16 Bank Holidays/days that the University is closed by custom (including Christmas) – That’s 42 days a year!
Generous pension scheme options plus life assurance
Health and Wellbeing: Discounted staff membership options at The Edge, our state-of-the-art Campus gym, with a pool, sauna, climbing wall, cycle circuit, and sports halls.

Research Associate - LGBTQ+ inclusion at work - (9701)

Manchester Metropolitan University is seeking an ambitious and talented Research Associate to join the Business School.

This twelve-month opportunity (likely from February/March 2027 to February/March 2028) will support the development of high-quality, internationally recognised research in the field of LGBTQ+ workplace inclusion.

Working closely with Professor Luke Fletcher in the Faculty of Business and Law, the successful candidate will contribute to fieldwork and qualitative data collection activities (and the writing up of analyses for journal publication) as well as supporting the development of a large research funding bid that builds from the project.

About the Role

The Research Associate will play a key role in advancing the University's research profile and Faculty's research priorities through leading fieldwork and data collection activities (mostly qualitative) as well as the writing up of analyses for academic publications and supporting a large research funding application. You will work collaboratively with senior academics while also taking responsibility for progressing independent research activities and contributing to the wider research culture of the People and Performance department.

Key responsibilities include:

Assisting with the design and planning of the project.
Leading the fieldwork and data collection activities and associated data recording/management processes.
Leading the advanced qualitative analysis of fieldwork data and writing up of the analysis for publication (both academic and policy/practice outputs).
Undertaking reviews or critical analyses of the literature where appropriate.
Supporting with the development and drafting of manuscripts for submission to highly ranked academic journals.
Supporting with the presentation of research findings at conferences, seminars, and research forums.
Supporting the development of external research funding applications.
Building and maintaining productive relationships with internal and external partners.
Contributing to the wider activities of the Business School where appropriate.

About You:

We are looking for a highly motivated researcher with expertise in qualitative fieldwork and advanced qualitative analytical methods and research interests in LGBTQ+ workplace inclusion. You will be committed to rigorous qualitative methods that centre lived experience as well as participatory and creative approaches, and to producing high-quality outputs and developing high-quality external research funding applications. We also would appreciate someone that can conduct expert (or subject matter expert) interviews (e.g., with senior managers, EDI professionals) as well as more participatory methods with LGBTQ+ groups and individuals.

You will have:

A doctoral qualification (or be close to completion) in a relevant discipline (e.g., organisational psychology or sociology of work, management/organisation studies, gender studies or LGBTQ+ studies, industrial relations).
Demonstrable breadth/depth of knowledge (and experience) about qualitative research design/methods/analysis
Ability to use initiative, creativity and judgement to develop appropriate approaches in order to further research.
Ability to plan, prioritise and organise work on multiple tasks.
Ability to synthesise complex data from different sources and communicate findings orally and via written reports and articles for a range of diverse audiences.
The ability to build productive relationships and research networks.

Desirable Criteria

In-depth knowledge about LGBTQ+ lives as it pertains to work and employment as well as EDI/DEI strategies and initiatives within organisations.
Specific knowledge around employment and equality law would be also be appreciated.
Demonstrable evidence of continuous professional development (e.g. undertaking additional research methods training or researcher skills development programmes)
Hold membership with the British Psychological Society or British Sociological Association where you adhere to their guidelines around ethical professional/research practice
Preparation of funding proposals and applications to external funders.
An emerging track record of publications in highly ranked journals.
Evidence of successful collaboration with external partners and stakeholders.
Experience presenting research findings at national and/or international conferences.
Experience with expert interviewing and/or participatory approaches to data collection.

Application & Assessment 

To apply, submit your CV and respond to a few set questions pertaining to specific criteria via our online portal. Please note applications received without answering all the pre-set questions will not be considered. 
Please provide a list of any publications, conference papers, grant/funding applications in your CV, regardless of their specific relevance to the topic area.
Please also provide information about doctorate level qualification in your CV, particularly if the thesis has been submitted but you are awaiting the viva/defense or are currently in a revision period (post viva).
Assessment will include a competency-based interview between 11th and 15th January 2027, ideally in-person at Manchester Metropolitan University.
Due to the volume of applications, we receive, we sometimes close our vacancies early. It is therefore advisable to apply as early as possible if you would like to be considered for a role.  
For informal enquiries about this vacancy, please contact Professor Luke Fletcher at l.fletcher@mmu.ac.uk 

 

Further Information 

Manchester Metropolitan University fosters an inclusive culture of belonging that promotes equity and celebrates diversity. We value a diverse workforce for the innovation and diversity of thought it brings and welcome applications from local and international communities, including those from Black, Asian, and Minority Ethnic backgrounds, disabled people, and LGBTQ+ individuals. 

We support a range of flexible working arrangements, including hybrid and tailored schedules, which can be discussed with your line manager. If you require reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process or in your role, please let us know so we can provide appropriate support. 

Our commitment to inclusivity includes mentoring programmes, accessibility resources, and professional development opportunities to empower and support underrepresented groups. 

Manchester Met is a Disability Confident Leader and, under this scheme, aims to offer an interview to disabled people who apply for the role and meet the essential criteria as listed in the attached Job Description for that vacancy. This vacancy is expected to attract a high volume of applications. Therefore, under the Disability Confident Scheme, only disabled people who apply under the scheme and best meet the essential criteria will be offered an interview.

 About us 

 There is a vacancy for a graduate Research Assistant to join a research group headed by Professor Alison Hardcastle. The Hardcastle lab fosters a collegiate and inclusive environment that works closely in a shared lab with several other PIs to form a large team (>30) at the UCL Institute of Ophthalmology.

 About the role 

 We are looking for a research assistant to differentiate retinal organoids which are used to explore the molecular mechanisms of retinal degeneration and test potential therapeutic approaches. The successful candidate will be motivated to contribute to high-quality research, with an ability to think and work independently and work effectively as part of team, with excellent organizational skills.

 About you 

 The post would suit an ambitious researcher with a strong interest in the mechanisms of neurodegeneration, retinal molecular and cellular biology, and/or therapeutic development. The successful candidate will preferably have experience of stem cell culture and differentiation. They will also have experience of immunohistochemistry, transcriptomics and biochemical analyses. They will work as part of a multidisciplinary team, and with established collaborators, to investigate the molecular mechanism of inherited retinal degeneration using iPSC derived retinal organoids and animal models to explore potential therapies.

 Applicants close to submission of their PhD will also be considered. Appointment as a Research Fellow at Grade 7 is dependent upon having been awarded a PhD. If this is not the case, an initial appointment will be made as a Research Assistant at Grade 6b (£39,807 -£41,833) with payment at Grade 7 backdated upon award of a PhD to the date of final submission of the PhD thesis (with corrections)
